note: Movements derived from the 40 distinct exercise names in IRONLOG_PROGRAM. Equipment and execution vocabularies follow the standard axes. Entries with review:true need a human ruling before migration.

movements.name: Triceps Pushdown
movements.reviewNote: Rope and straight bar are merged here — same equipment, different attachment. You log them at different loads (rope 34-38, bar 32-40), so merging loses that. Either accept it, split them into two movements, or add attachment as a fourth axis. Attachment as an axis is the tidiest but the most work.

movements.name: Bench Press
movements.reviewNote: Biggest call in the file. Merging Machine Chest Press and Flat DB Press into Bench Press as equipment variants is the compression the model exists for, and PRs stay separate per leaf. But a seated machine press is arguably a different movement pattern from a flat barbell bench. Split them if you disagree.

movements.name: Calf Raise (standing)
movements.reviewNote: Your most-logged movement, 113 prescribed sets. Standing and seated calf raise are separate movements (seated biases soleus), so keep this one standing-only and add a seated entry if you train it. Also check whether your Smith work is loaded plus bar weight or plates only, since that changes every historical number.

movements.name: Leg Curl
movements.reviewNote: Seated and lying leg curl are different machines with different strength curves. If you use both, split them — otherwise the PR is meaningless.

movements.name: Lateral Raise
movements.reviewNote: Your cable version logs 10-11.3 kg and the dumbbell version 12.5 kg. If the cable work is single-arm it should default to unilateral, which changes the load convention to per-side and makes the two comparable. Confirm how you actually do it.
